overview: Artemis is the only anticheat with real logic on the resource-pack-status packet. Its PingSpoofProtocol uses the packet as a cheap keepalive on 1.8 servers to detect ping spoofing, and ResourcePackTickHandler turns it into a tick-confirmation channel. Other corpus hits are packet-type registrations and FlopAC wrappers.

checks.name: PingSpoofProtocol (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Detect ping spoofing using resource-pack responses as keepalives.
checks.how_it_works: On 1.9 and older servers, the check pushes a fake resource pack whose URL encodes a numeric id, then expects the client's ResourcePackStatus response with FAILED_DOWNLOAD and a matching id, followed by the next keepalive. Missing, out-of-order, or non-numeric responses log violations. On 1.10+ it switches to fake teleports because the resource-pack hash was removed.
checks.detects: Ping spoofers that suppress or reorder keepalive packets, and clients that answer resource-pack requests they were never sent.
checks.variations: ResourcePackTickHandler in the same repo reuses the mechanism as a tick-confirmation channel on 1.8; FlopAC and Negativity only register the packet type.

checks.name: ResourcePackTickHandler (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Turn resource-pack status into a tick counter for the connection.
checks.how_it_works: On 1.8 servers, pushes a level:// resource pack whose hash encodes a numeric id, and accepts only FAILED_DOWNLOAD responses whose URL is numeric and contains the player name. The parsed id is stored as the player's resourcePackTick.
checks.detects: Nothing directly. It feeds the tick-confirmation infrastructure that other Artemis checks use to measure connection state.
checks.variations: PingSpoofProtocol is the same mechanism used for keepalive verification; the tick handler is the non-checking consumer of it.
